decisive_items: brownish macules on the hands and feet
multiple type II and III Yamada polyps on atrophic gastric mucosa
response.rationale: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome is strongly suggested by the combination of mucocutaneous pigmentation (brownish macules on hands/feet, hyperchromic punctate lesions) and multiple GI polyps, along with a history of cleft lip/palate repair. The other conditions lack these characteristic skin findings and polyp distribution.

rejected.why: Juvenile polyposis syndrome also presents with GI polyps but typically lacks the mucocutaneous pigmentation and cleft lip/palate association seen here.
Autoimmune enteropathy would cause diarrhea and malabsorption but not polyps or skin pigmentation.
Celiac disease causes diarrhea and malabsorption but is not associated with polyps or the specific skin lesions.
Crohn's disease can cause diarrhea and abdominal pain but typically shows ulcerations and skip lesions, not polyps, and lacks the skin findings.
